findings.claim: The export promises an input to R29 without KW's induction, but directly imports the proved R27.6/full-classical-serre-theorem and R27.6/finite-flat-weight-two-export. The latter also depends on the former. Thus its executable prerequisite plan imports the classical proof rather than only a StrongSerre statement/theorem parameter. This is a dependency error, not a false finite-flat consequence.
findings.evidence: The node says 'the export is stated as a function of StrongSerre (a theorem parameter)' but the shortest explicit path is R33.6/elliptic-curve-export-via-either-route -> R27.6/full-classical-serre-theorem -> R27.4/theorem-1-2 -> R27.3/double-induction-assembly. R27.3's packet contains all three latter nodes. The alternative path through R27.6/finite-flat-weight-two-export reaches the same theorem. Its internal closure has 34 R26/R27.2-R27.6 nodes; the modern strong theorem has only the minimal-lifts node. The R33.6 roadmap explicitly requires the R29 consequence 'through a theorem parameter or a separate corollary'.
findings.fix: Keep one owned StrongSerre proposition/interface, separate from either proof. Make a shared finite-flat consequence conditional on that proposition, with the local weight recipe and Carayol change-of-nebentypus imports explicit; instantiate it with the modern strong proof here. Remove both unconditional classical-proof edges. Reuse/generalise the owned R27.6 export instead of duplicating its mathematical argument, coordinating that supplier change if needed. Add an acceptance check of the modern export's closure, not merely its prose: no classical induction or level-one proof may be reached.

findings.where: research/blueprint/packets/ClassicalSerreModularity--R33.5.json: R33.5/auxiliary-odd-prime-for-the-dyadic-system, fourth hypothesis and second proof step
findings.claim: For the node's arbitrary almost strictly compatible system through a dyadic lift, the assertion that a reducible p-adic member makes the 2-adic member reducible 'by Chebotarev and Brauer-Nesbitt' omits the construction of 2-adic companions of its two characters. Those theorems compare continuous representations in a common coefficient characteristic; equality of compatible Frobenius polynomials does not itself supply those companions. The proposed irreducibility conclusion is not being asserted false. The narrower KW-constructed system has the needed property explicitly, and suffices for the application.
findings.evidence: DP v2 p. 7 Definition 1.10(4) gives semisimple members over K_p; Theorem 1.11 promises an almost strictly compatible system. In Remark 4 on that page the source first constructs Deligne's system for the modular form, and only then compares the two members at the same prime by Brauer-Nesbitt. In contrast the target proof step changes from a reducible p-adic member to the 2-adic lift without a rank-one companion construction. KW I p. 8 defines irreducible to mean every member is irreducible, and p. 9 Theorem 5.1 explicitly promises an 'irreducible, odd system'. The current R24.6/residual-members node assumes such a system; it does not prove characteristic-zero irreducibility from one member.
findings.fix: Either restrict the auxiliary lemma to the irreducible odd system supplied by KW I Theorem 5.1 (current supplier node R24.5/kw-theorem-5-1-systems), which still gives the dyadic closure, or explicitly import/request the rank-one geometric-character comparison from R24: classify the de Rham finitely ramified characters over Q, construct their companions at 2 and the compatible determinant, then apply Chebotarev/Brauer-Nesbitt at 2. Do not leave the arbitrary-system conclusion justified by cross-characteristic Brauer-Nesbitt alone. Preserve the distinction between characteristic-zero irreducibility and possibly reducible residual members.

findings.claim: Several broad stage imports no longer satisfy PROTOCOL section 3's 'only when no finer node exists yet' rule. In particular the R24.6 request conflates existence of a system, now planned in R24.5, with transfer of modularity, planned in R24.6. The R32.6 gap is described without linking the existing partial audit, and the comparison bypasses the existing exact 'arises from' definition. This hides the usable supplier interfaces and the remaining obligations.
findings.evidence: Current finer nodes read in full or by their complete statement/hypotheses: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.3/theorem-5-1-part-1-minimal-crystalline and /theorem-5-1-part-2-weight-two; R24.5/dieulefait-families ('rho is part of a rank-2 almost strictly compatible system') or /kw-theorem-5-1-systems; R24.6/linked-systems-modularity-transfer ('a compatible system is modular if and only if one of its members is'); GL2ModularityLifting:R32.6/globalisation-dependency-audit, whose hypotheses explicitly retain unaudited global inputs; AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.6/s-type-arises-from-and-modular, which gives the exact coefficient-place/newform definition and invariance. All are present in the repository snapshot a172a5d. PROTOCOL section 3 says to use the supplying node's id when it exists.
findings.fix: Replace each covered stage edge with the exact supplying node(s), split the system-existence request from the modularity-transfer request, and link the partial globalisation audit while retaining its actual unresolved requirements as a gap. Use the existing S-type/arises-from node for the comparison, leaving the eigenform/newform comparison itself here. Do not mark unreviewed/partial suppliers proved or close requests whose statements are not fully supplied; keep R17.6 and any genuinely unmatched optimisation need explicit. These are current-snapshot updates, not a claim that the original worker ignored nodes before they existed.

findings.claim: The README still says the modern route stops being independent of KW 'exactly' at the scalar dyadic case, although the independent review explicitly rejected and corrected that wording in the packet. The planned refinement uses KW minimal lifts/lifting for every odd-prime and dyadic weight-two case. Its source-issues paragraph also stops at E3-E7 although the revised nodes cite E9.

The packet's review.checked entry for R33.6/two-routes-comparison explains that the route already uses Theorem 5.1, and as planned uses R27.4/strong-form-by-minimal-lifts for the refinement. The corrected node distinguishes that use from the scalar case being the one where the KW refinement was indispensable. KW I p. 2 section 1.1 identifies the missing scalar characteristic-two case; DP p. 6 attributes its initial lifts to KW. Both revised strong-form/comparison nodes cite ClassicalSerreModularity/E9 in part R27.3.
findings.fix: Synchronise the README with the reviewed JSON: independence of the qualitative induction, shared KW lift-existence inputs, the chosen minimal-lift refinement in the stated branches, and historical indispensability in the scalar dyadic case are distinct claims. Update the source-issues cross-reference to include E9 while retaining that this part found no new source issue.

findings.claim: The preamble's assertion that 'Galois representations and modular forms are not in the pinned libraries' is too broad: modular forms and cusp forms already exist in pinned Mathlib, and Tau Ceti has substantial newform theory. The missing Serre/Galois-modularity interface justifies leaving these theorem signatures schematic, but absence of modular forms does not.
findings.evidence: Read at Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174, Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Basic.lean lines 74-84: structures ModularForm and CuspForm extend SlashInvariantForm Gamma k, with holomorphy and bounded/zero-at-cusps fields. At Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369, TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/Basic.lean defines cuspFormsOld, and Newforms/StrongMultiplicityOne.lean lines 87-91 states HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.eq_of_forall_notMem_eigenvalue_eq for Newform N k, fixed nebentypus and equal good-index eigenvalues outside a finite set. The reviewed R27.6 library audit likewise says existing newforms give the target objects.
findings.fix: Qualify the note to the unavailable residual Galois-representation/modularity interface and reuse the existing modular-form/newform carriers when developing it. Keep the missing theorem signatures commented; neither these positive declarations nor the finite examples imply that Serre's theorem is formalised.
